meaning: Detection of the jugular "créneau" (step plateau) requires at least one supra-threshold run longer than 20 s on the 10 s smoothed trace; if none is found the preparation aborts instead of falling back. The threshold is fixed at halfway between baseline and the signal maximum.

could_move.what: The 20 s minimum duration: recordings with a shorter or interrupted plateau raise instead of yielding a window, so those patients silently drop out of the fitted set.
The 50% of (max - baseline) threshold uses nanmax, so a single spike or artefact raises thr and can shrink or erase the detected segment.
Only the longest segment is kept; if the step is split by a dropout, the retained window is a fragment and the later 1 s edge refinement starts from the wrong edges.

expectation: Unknown. It changes which recordings enter the fit and the window boundaries, not the model equations. Whether any current patient sits near the 20 s or 50% boundary cannot be told from this context.

check.why: Runs the preparation only and shows whether any recording hits the RuntimeError or produces a suspiciously short window, without re-fitting.
